elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Rendered grant: "The Servicer grants the Issuer and the Depositor, and on written notice their Affiliates, a license to use its processes, procedures, models, servicing software and other applications ..." — Affiliates of the Issuer/Depositor (our side) are within the grant.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant names only "the Issuer and the Depositor, and on written notice their Affiliates"; no reference to contractors, subcontractors, agents or service providers acting on our behalf appears anywhere in the rendered sentence.
The grant carries no duration term at all ("a license to use ... as necessary to service the Receivables"); the word "perpetual" and any paid-up-licence concept are absent.
No "irrevocable" (or equivalent non-revocation) wording in the rendered grant; the licence is silent on revocation, so nothing bars withdrawal at the Servicer's instance.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The rendered sentence contains no termination standard for the licence; there is no "only for material breach that remains uncured" limitation, and the licence's scope ("as necessary to service the Receivables") does not supply one.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: The clause says "transferable to a successor by merger or acquisition" only — a narrower subset than successors generally (e.g., successors by asset sale, reorganisation or operation of law are not covered). Read literally, the M&A-limited wording does not deliver the unqualified preferred element.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "grants the Issuer and the Depositor, and on written notice their Affiliates, a license to use ..." — affiliate coverage is expressly conditioned on written notice, exactly the fallback mechanic. (Issuer/Depositor as defined do not already subsume affiliates, so there is no duplicate coverage.)

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "... as necessary to service the Receivables, transferable to a successor by merger or acquisition" — express M&A successor transferability, and the deleted blanket "will not be obligated to ... license or assign ... to any ... third party" no longer contradicts it.

reasons: Fallback is complete: both fallback elements are met in operative language (affiliates on written notice; transferability to a successor by merger or acquisition), and no at-will revocation survives. The finding is correctly pitched at the fallback and correctly classified as a deviation, since the original sentence granted no rights at all and foreclosed any path to affiliate coverage.

Preferred is not complete: contractor coverage, perpetuity, irrevocability, termination-only-for-uncured-material-breach, and unqualified successor transferability are all absent. If the preferred level is ever pursued, add "and their contractors acting on their behalf", "perpetual and irrevocable" for paid-up rights, a "terminable only on uncured material breach" limitation, and drop the "by merger or acquisition" qualifier.

Minimality fails on the deletion beyond the reconciliation actually required. Only the "or any third party" reach of the old disclaimer contradicted the new grant; the drafter also struck "license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer", removing a Servicer protection that sits outside both fallback elements and that governs the Successor Servicer transition allocation in Section 7.4/7.5. Repair: restore that carve-out in narrowed form, e.g. "; provided further that, except as granted above, the Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer, or provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies."

The margin comment/rationale overstates the position by asserting that Section 7.4's transition/IP allocation is "otherwise untouched"; the struck Successor Servicer language is precisely that allocation. Align the comment with the operative edit once the carve-out is restored.

Intent is otherwise preserved: no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence, the legal/regulatory/confidentiality carve-out survives, and the delivery obligations in clause (ii) are unaffected. One drafting check: confirm "Affiliates" is a defined term in the Transfer and Servicing Agreement (it is not in the supplied definition set); if not, add a definition or use "affiliates" descriptively to avoid an undefined capitalised term.

Scope note (not a defect at the fallback): the licence is limited to use "as necessary to service the Receivables", which may be narrow given the Issuer/Depositor do not themselves service; consider "as necessary to service, or to have serviced, the Receivables" if broader utility is needed.
